Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 18, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

Al-Qurtubi said: It is Meccan according to the agreement of all the exegetes (mufassirun).

It is narrated from a group that the beginning of the surah was revealed in Medina, up to His saying ﴿jurzan﴾ (barren). But the first view is more sound. End of quotation.

Among those who said that the whole surah is Meccan is Ibn 'Abbas, which al-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him. Among them also is Ibn al-Zubayr, which Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him.

Hadiths have come concerning its virtue, among them what Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and others transmitted from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever memorises ten verses from the beginning of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal (the Antichrist)."

Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Hibban transmitted, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the last ten verses of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal."

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others transmitted, from al-Bara', who said: "A man recited Surat al-Kahf while there was an animal in the house, and it began to shy. He looked and saw a mist or a cloud that had covered him. He mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'Recite, so-and-so, for tranquillity (sakinah) descended for the Qur'an.'" This man who was reciting was Usayd ibn Hudayr, as al-Tabarani made clear.

al-Tirmidhi transmitted and graded it sound, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites three verses from the beginning of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal." Regarding the recitation of ten verses from its beginning or from its end, there are hadiths.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah transmitted, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites al-Kahf on Friday, he is protected until eight days from every trial that occurs. If the Dajjal emerges, he will be protected from him."

al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Hakim (who graded it sound), Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi and al-Diya' transmitted, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf, it will be a light for him from his station to Makkah. Whoever recites ten verses from its end, then the Dajjal emerges, he will not harm him."

al-Hakim transmitted and graded it sound, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf on the day of Friday, there will be light shining for him between the two Fridays."

al-Bayhaqi also transmitted it in al-Sunan from this route and from another route.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf on the day of Friday, a light will shine for him from beneath his foot up to the clouds of the sky, illuminating for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be forgiven what is between the two Fridays."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I inform you of a surah whose greatness fills what is between the heaven and the earth, and for its writer is a reward like that? Whoever recites it on Friday, he will be forgiven what is between him and the next Friday, with an addition of three days. And whoever recites its last five verses when he sleeps, Allah will raise him at whatever hour of the night he wishes." They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "The surah of the People of the Cave."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The house in which Surat al-Kahf is recited, a devil will not enter it that night." There are other hadiths and reports on this subject, and what we have cited is sufficient.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿All praise belongs to Allah, who sent down the Book to His servant and did not make in it any crookedness﴾ ﴿a upright (qayyim) [book], to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good news to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward﴾ ﴿remaining therein forever﴾ ﴿and to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."﴾ ﴿They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they say nothing but a lie.﴾ ﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief over their footsteps if they do not believe in this message.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed.﴾ ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it into barren dust.﴾

He taught His servants how to praise Him for the bounties He pours upon them. The description with the relative pronoun indicates that what is in the relative clause is the cause of what precedes it. The reason that the sending down of the Book, which is the Qur'an, is a blessing upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is that through it he came to know the secrets of monotheism (tawhid), the conditions of the angels and the prophets, and the manner of the legal rulings (ahkam shar'iyyah) by which Allah worshipped him and worshipped his community. Likewise, for the servants, the sending down of the Book upon their prophet was a blessing for them, for the same reason we have mentioned concerning the Prophet.

﴿And did not make in it any crookedness (iwaj)﴾, meaning: no crookedness of any kind of defect in wording or meaning. The word ﴿iwaj﴾ with a kasra (ʿiwaj) is used for meanings, and with a fatha (ʿawaj) for physical things. So it has been said, and it is objected to by His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿You will not see in it any crookedness or unevenness﴾ [Ta-Ha: 107], meaning the mountains, which are physical things.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning in the verse is: He did not place in it any contradiction, as He said: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction﴾ [al-Nisa': 82].

And qayyim means: the straight one that has no deviation; or the one that manages the religious and worldly welfare of the servants; or the one that is a guardian over the heavenly books before it, dominating them. According to the first meaning, it is an emphasis of what the negation of crookedness indicates, for something that appears straight may not be free of the slightest crookedness in reality. The accusative of ﴿qayyiman﴾ is by a hidden verb, meaning: He made it qayyim. The author of al-Kashshaf (Zamakhshari's commentary) prevented it from being a circumstantial state (hal) of "the Book," because His saying ﴿and did not make﴾ is conjoined to ﴿sent down﴾, so it falls within the scope of the relative clause; thus making it a state of "the Book" would separate the state from its owner by part of the relative clause.

Al-Isfahani said: They are two successive states, except that the first is a clause and the second is a single word. This is correct, because His saying ﴿and did not make﴾ was not conjoined to what precedes it; rather the waw is for the state, so there is no separation between the state and its owner by part of the relative clause.

It has also been said that ﴿qayyiman﴾ is a state of the pronoun in ﴿did not make for Him﴾. And it has been said: in the speech there is a fronting and deferring, and the estimate is: He sent down upon His servant the Book, upright, and did not make for Him crookedness. Then He, glory be to Him, wished to explain what He had summarised in His saying ﴿qayyiman﴾, so He said: ﴿to warn of severe punishment﴾. The one warned is omitted for knowledge of him together with the intention of generality; the meaning is: to warn the disbelievers.

The ﴿ba's (بَأْسًا)﴾ means punishment, and the meaning of ﴿min ladunhu﴾ is: proceeding from Him, descending from His presence.

Abu Bakr narrated from 'Asim that he recited ﴿min ladunihi﴾ (مِن لَدُنِهِ) with a hint of the dammah on the dal, and with a kasra on the nun and the ha'. This is the dialect of the Kilab.

Abu Zayd narrated from all the readers the fatha on the lam, the damma on the dal, and sukun on the nun (مِن لَدُنْهُ). ﴿And gives good news to the believers who do righteous deeds﴾: it has been read ﴿yubashshiru﴾ with tashdid and with takhfif, and the relative clause was given the same relative clause mentioned earlier, because the basis of the acceptance of deeds is faith. ﴿That they will have a good reward﴾, which is Paradise, while they are ﴿remaining therein﴾, meaning: in that reward, ﴿forever﴾, meaning: a lasting stay with no cessation. The placing of the warning before the good news is to show complete concern for restraining the disbelievers.

Then He repeated the warning and mentioned the one warned specifically, and omitted what is warned of, which is the severe punishment, since it had already been mentioned. He said: ﴿and to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."﴾ They are the Jews, the Christians, and some of the disbelievers of Quraysh, who say that the angels are the daughters of Allah. So He, glory be to Him, first mentioned a universal proposition, which is the warning of disbelievers in general, then He followed it with a specific proposition which is a part of the particulars of that universal, to draw attention to it being the greatest of the particulars of that universal. This indicates that attributing a son to Allah, glory be to Him, is the most hideous kind of disbelief.

﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾, meaning: of the son, or of Allah taking him. The ﴿min (مِن)﴾ is extra for emphasis of the negation, and the clause is in a place of accusative as a state, or it is a new sentence; the meaning is: they have no knowledge of that at all. ﴿Nor did their fathers﴾ have knowledge; rather, in this claim of theirs they were in error, and their children imitated them, so they all went astray. ﴿Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾: the accusative of ﴿kalimatan (كَلِمَةً)﴾ is as a specification (tamyiz), and it has been read in the nominative as the subject.

Al-Farra' said: That word was great as a word.

Al-Zajjaj said: Their statement was great as a word, and what is meant by this word is their saying: "Allah has taken a son."

Then He described the word with His saying ﴿that comes out of their mouths﴾, and the benefit of this description is to magnify their audacity in uttering it. What comes out of the mouth is only mere breath, but since letters and sounds are qualities subsisting in the breath, He attributed to the state what belongs to the place. Then He increased in disparaging what had occurred from them and said: ﴿they say nothing but a lie﴾, meaning: they say nothing but a lie with no room for truth in it in any way.

Then He consoled His Messenger (ﷺ) with His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief over their footsteps.﴾ Al-Akhfash and al-Farra' said: al-bakhʿ (البَخْعُ) is exertion.

Al-Kisa'i said: I exhausted the land by farming when you make it weak through continuous ploughing, and the man exhausted himself when he wore it out.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: its meaning is: destroying yourself, and from it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: "O you, the one whom grief has destroyed (al-bakhi' al-wajd) himself." So the meaning according to these statements is: perhaps you would exhaust yourself, or weaken it, or destroy it, over their footsteps, meaning after their departure and after their turning away and aversion, ﴿if they do not believe in this message﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. The answer of the condition is omitted, and what precedes it indicates it.

It has been read with fatha on the ﴿an (أنْ)﴾, meaning: because they did not believe, ﴿out of grief (asafan)﴾, meaning: anger and sorrow. It is either an object of purpose or a verbal noun in the place of a state. So said al-Zajjaj.

﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it﴾: this sentence is a new beginning.

The meaning is: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth, of what is fit to be an adornment for it, of animals, plants, and inanimate things, as in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿He it is who created for you all that is on the earth﴾. The accusative of ﴿zinatan (زِينَةً)﴾ is that it is the second object of ﴿ja'ala (جَعَلَ)﴾. The lam in ﴿that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed﴾ is connected to ﴿ja'alna (جَعَلْنا)﴾, and it is either for purpose or for consequence. What is meant by the trial is that He, glory be to Him, treats them with a treatment which, if it came from other than Him, would be of the kind of trial and examination.

Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿Ayyuhum (أيُّهم)﴾ is raised as the subject, except that its form is the form of a question, and the meaning is: that We may examine: is this one better in deed, or that one? Al-Hasan said: ﴿ayyuhum (أيُّهم)﴾ means: which of them is more ascetic. Muqatil said: which of them is most righteous in what he has been given of knowledge.

Then He, glory be to Him, informed that He will annihilate and destroy all of that, so He said: ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it into barren dust (sa'idan juruzan)﴾, meaning: indeed, We will make what is upon it of this adornment, at the end of the life of this world, into dust.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-sa'id (الصَّعِيدُ) is the level of the earth.

Al-Zajjaj said: It is the road which has no vegetation in it.

Al-Farra' said: al-juruz (الجُرُزُ) is the land in which there is no vegetation. From their saying: a woman who is jurraz (جُرازٌ) when she is a great eater; a sword which is jurraz when it is cutting off completely; and the locust, the sheep and the camels "jarazat" the land when they have eaten what is on it.

Dhu al-Rummah said: "The pressing and the grazing (al-ijraz) have emptied what is in their bellies."

The meaning of the structure is: Do not grieve, O Muhammad, over what has happened from these people of denial. Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for the testing of their deeds, and indeed, We will remove that at the completion of the life of this world, and We will recompense them: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.

Al-Shawkani, Fath al-Qadir, on Surah 18, verses 1–8 (part 2 of 2):

It has been related by Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh, through the chain of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who sent down to His servant the Book﴾ (the verse), that he said: He sent down the Book as "upright" (ʿadlan qayyiman), ﴿and has not made in it any deviance﴾ meaning, ambiguity (multabisan).

Ibn al-Mundhir related from al-Dahhak regarding (qayyiman) that he said: "Straight" (mustaqiman).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah regarding (min ladunhu) that it means: from Him (min ʿindihi).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi regarding (hasanan), meaning Paradise, ﴿and to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son"﴾. He said: They are the Jews and the Christians.

Ibn Mardawayh also related, "from Ibn Abbas, who said: ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabiʿah, Abu Jahl, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib and Abu al-Bukhturi gathered with a group of the Quraysh, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been deeply grieved by what he saw of his people's opposition to him and their rejection of the counsel he brought, which saddened him greatly. Thereupon Allah, glorified is He, sent down: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them﴾."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding (bakhiʿun nafsaka) that it means: "Killing yourself" (qatilun nafsaka).

ʿAbd ibn Humayd related from Mujahid the like of this, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi the like of this.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid regarding (asafan) that he said: "Distress" (jazʿan).

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah regarding (asafan) that he said: "Sorrow" (huznan).

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh related, through the chain of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is upon the earth an adornment for it﴾, that he said: "The men."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from his own statement, the like of this.

Abu Nasr al-Sijzi in al-Ibanah related, through the chain of Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "The scholars are the adornment of the earth."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan who said: They are the men who worship and labor for Allah through obedience.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim in al-Tarikh and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Umar who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿That He may test you [as to] which of you is best in deed﴾. I said: 'What is the meaning of that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'That He may test you as to which of you is best in intellect, most scrupulous regarding the prohibitions of Allah, and quickest in obedience to Allah.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah who said: "to test them" (liyakhtabirahum), ﴿which of them is best in deed﴾: "which of them is most complete in intellect."

He related from al-Hasan, ﴿which of them is best in deed﴾, who said: "The one most abstaining from this world," and he also related from al-Thawri who said: "The most ascetic of them in this world."

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it a barren wasteland (saʿidan juruzan)﴾, that he said: "He destroys everything and annihilates it."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah who said: "The saʿid is the dust, and the mountains in which there is no crop."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan who said: "By juruz he means the ruined."

This indicates that attributing a son to Allah, glory be to Him, is the most hideous kind of disbelief.

﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾, meaning: of the son, or of Allah taking him. The ﴿min (مِن)﴾ is extra for emphasis of the negation, and the clause is in a place of accusative as a state, or it is a new sentence; the meaning is: they have no knowledge of that at all. ﴿Nor did their fathers﴾ have knowledge; rather, in this claim of theirs they were in error, and their children imitated them, so they all went astray. ﴿Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾: the accusative of ﴿kalimatan (كَلِمَةً)﴾ is as a specification (tamyiz), and it has been read in the nominative as the subject.

Al-Farra' said: That word was great as a word.

Al-Zajjaj said: Their statement was great as a word, and what is meant by this word is their saying: "Allah has taken a son."

Then He described the word with His saying ﴿that comes out of their mouths﴾, and the benefit of this description is to magnify their audacity in uttering it. What comes out of the mouth is only mere breath, but since letters and sounds are qualities subsisting in the breath, He attributed to the state what belongs to the place. Then He increased in disparaging what had occurred from them and said: ﴿they say nothing but a lie﴾, meaning: they say nothing but a lie with no room for truth in it in any way.

Then He consoled His Messenger (ﷺ) with His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief over their footsteps.﴾ Al-Akhfash and al-Farra' said: al-bakhʿ (البَخْعُ) is exertion.

Al-Kisa'i said: I exhausted the land by farming when you make it weak through continuous ploughing, and the man exhausted himself when he wore it out.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: its meaning is: destroying yourself, and from it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: "O you, the one whom grief has destroyed (al-bakhi' al-wajd) himself." So the meaning according to these statements is: perhaps you would exhaust yourself, or weaken it, or destroy it, over their footsteps, meaning after their departure and after their turning away and aversion, ﴿if they do not believe in this message﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. The answer of the condition is omitted, and what precedes it indicates it.

It has been read with fatha on the ﴿an (أنْ)﴾, meaning: because they did not believe, ﴿out of grief (asafan)﴾, meaning: anger and sorrow. It is either an object of purpose or a verbal noun in the place of a state. So said al-Zajjaj.

﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it﴾: this sentence is a new beginning.

The meaning is: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth, of what is fit to be an adornment for it, of animals, plants, and inanimate things, as in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿He it is who created for you all that is on the earth﴾. The accusative of ﴿zinatan (زِينَةً)﴾ is that it is the second object of ﴿ja'ala (جَعَلَ)﴾. The lam in ﴿that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed﴾ is connected to ﴿ja'alna (جَعَلْنا)﴾, and it is either for purpose or for consequence. What is meant by the trial is that He, glory be to Him, treats them with a treatment which, if it came from other than Him, would be of the kind of trial and examination.

Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿Ayyuhum (أيُّهم)﴾ is raised as the subject, except that its form is the form of a question, and the meaning is: that We may examine: is this one better in deed, or that one? Al-Hasan said: ﴿ayyuhum (أيُّهم)﴾ means: which of them is more ascetic. Muqatil said: which of them is most righteous in what he has been given of knowledge.

Then He, glory be to Him, informed that He will annihilate and destroy all of that, so He said: ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it into barren dust (sa'idan juruzan)﴾, meaning: indeed, We will make what is upon it of this adornment, at the end of the life of this world, into dust.

Al-Zajjaj said: It is the road which has no vegetation in it.

Al-Shawkani, Fath al-Qadir, on Surah 18, verses 1–8 (part 2 of 2):

It has been related by Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh, through the chain of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who sent down to His servant the Book﴾ (the verse), that he said: He sent down the Book as "upright" (ʿadlan qayyiman), ﴿and has not made in it any deviance﴾ meaning, ambiguity (multabisan).

Ibn al-Mundhir related from al-Dahhak regarding (qayyiman) that he said: "Straight" (mustaqiman).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah regarding (min ladunhu) that it means: from Him (min ʿindihi).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi regarding (hasanan), meaning Paradise, ﴿and to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son"﴾. He said: They are the Jews and the Christians.

Ibn Mardawayh also related, "from Ibn Abbas, who said: ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabiʿah, Abu Jahl, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib and Abu al-Bukhturi gathered with a group of the Quraysh, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been deeply grieved by what he saw of his people's opposition to him and their rejection of the counsel he brought, which saddened him greatly. Thereupon Allah, glorified is He, sent down: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them﴾."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding (bakhiʿun nafsaka) that it means: "Killing yourself" (qatilun nafsaka).

ʿAbd ibn Humayd related from Mujahid the like of this, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi the like of this.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid regarding (asafan) that he said: "Distress" (jazʿan).

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah regarding (asafan) that he said: "Sorrow" (huznan).

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh related, through the chain of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is upon the earth an adornment for it﴾, that he said: "The men."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from his own statement, the like of this.

Abu Nasr al-Sijzi in al-Ibanah related, through the chain of Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "The scholars are the adornment of the earth."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan who said: They are the men who worship and labor for Allah through obedience.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim in al-Tarikh and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Umar who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿That He may test you [as to] which of you is best in deed﴾. I said: 'What is the meaning of that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'That He may test you as to which of you is best in intellect, most scrupulous regarding the prohibitions of Allah, and quickest in obedience to Allah.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah who said: "to test them" (liyakhtabirahum), ﴿which of them is best in deed﴾: "which of them is most complete in intellect."

He related from al-Hasan, ﴿which of them is best in deed﴾, who said: "The one most abstaining from this world," and he also related from al-Thawri who said: "The most ascetic of them in this world."

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it a barren wasteland (saʿidan juruzan)﴾, that he said: "He destroys everything and annihilates it."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah who said: "The saʿid is the dust, and the mountains in which there is no crop."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan who said: "By juruz he means the ruined."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 18, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

Al-Qurtubi said: It is Meccan according to the agreement of all the exegetes (mufassirun).

It is narrated from a group that the beginning of the surah was revealed in Medina, up to His saying ﴿jurzan﴾ (barren). But the first view is more sound. End of quotation.

Among those who said that the whole surah is Meccan is Ibn 'Abbas, which al-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him. Among them also is Ibn al-Zubayr, which Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him.

Hadiths have come concerning its virtue, among them what Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and others transmitted from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever memorises ten verses from the beginning of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal (the Antichrist)."

Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Hibban transmitted, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the last ten verses of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal."

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others transmitted, from al-Bara', who said: "A man recited Surat al-Kahf while there was an animal in the house, and it began to shy. He looked and saw a mist or a cloud that had covered him. He mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'Recite, so-and-so, for tranquillity (sakinah) descended for the Qur'an.'" This man who was reciting was Usayd ibn Hudayr, as al-Tabarani made clear.

al-Tirmidhi transmitted and graded it sound, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites three verses from the beginning of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal." Regarding the recitation of ten verses from its beginning or from its end, there are hadiths.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah transmitted, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites al-Kahf on Friday, he is protected until eight days from every trial that occurs. If the Dajjal emerges, he will be protected from him."

al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Hakim (who graded it sound), Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi and al-Diya' transmitted, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf, it will be a light for him from his station to Makkah. Whoever recites ten verses from its end, then the Dajjal emerges, he will not harm him."

al-Hakim transmitted and graded it sound, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf on the day of Friday, there will be light shining for him between the two Fridays."

al-Bayhaqi also transmitted it in al-Sunan from this route and from another route.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf on the day of Friday, a light will shine for him from beneath his foot up to the clouds of the sky, illuminating for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be forgiven what is between the two Fridays."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I inform you of a surah whose greatness fills what is between the heaven and the earth, and for its writer is a reward like that? Whoever recites it on Friday, he will be forgiven what is between him and the next Friday, with an addition of three days. And whoever recites its last five verses when he sleeps, Allah will raise him at whatever hour of the night he wishes." They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "The surah of the People of the Cave."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The house in which Surat al-Kahf is recited, a devil will not enter it that night." There are other hadiths and reports on this subject, and what we have cited is sufficient.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿All praise belongs to Allah, who sent down the Book to His servant and did not make in it any crookedness﴾ ﴿a upright (qayyim) [book], to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good news to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward﴾ ﴿remaining therein forever﴾ ﴿and to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."﴾ ﴿They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they say nothing but a lie.﴾ ﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief over their footsteps if they do not believe in this message.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed.﴾ ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it into barren dust.﴾

He taught His servants how to praise Him for the bounties He pours upon them. The description with the relative pronoun indicates that what is in the relative clause is the cause of what precedes it. The reason that the sending down of the Book, which is the Qur'an, is a blessing upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is that through it he came to know the secrets of monotheism (tawhid), the conditions of the angels and the prophets, and the manner of the legal rulings (ahkam shar'iyyah) by which Allah worshipped him and worshipped his community. Likewise, for the servants, the sending down of the Book upon their prophet was a blessing for them, for the same reason we have mentioned concerning the Prophet.

﴿And did not make in it any crookedness (iwaj)﴾, meaning: no crookedness of any kind of defect in wording or meaning. The word ﴿iwaj﴾ with a kasra (ʿiwaj) is used for meanings, and with a fatha (ʿawaj) for physical things. So it has been said, and it is objected to by His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿You will not see in it any crookedness or unevenness﴾ [Ta-Ha: 107], meaning the mountains, which are physical things.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning in the verse is: He did not place in it any contradiction, as He said: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction﴾ [al-Nisa': 82].

And qayyim means: the straight one that has no deviation; or the one that manages the religious and worldly welfare of the servants; or the one that is a guardian over the heavenly books before it, dominating them. According to the first meaning, it is an emphasis of what the negation of crookedness indicates, for something that appears straight may not be free of the slightest crookedness in reality. The accusative of ﴿qayyiman﴾ is by a hidden verb, meaning: He made it qayyim. The author of al-Kashshaf (Zamakhshari's commentary) prevented it from being a circumstantial state (hal) of "the Book," because His saying ﴿and did not make﴾ is conjoined to ﴿sent down﴾, so it falls within the scope of the relative clause; thus making it a state of "the Book" would separate the state from its owner by part of the relative clause.

Al-Isfahani said: They are two successive states, except that the first is a clause and the second is a single word. This is correct, because His saying ﴿and did not make﴾ was not conjoined to what precedes it; rather the waw is for the state, so there is no separation between the state and its owner by part of the relative clause.

It has also been said that ﴿qayyiman﴾ is a state of the pronoun in ﴿did not make for Him﴾. And it has been said: in the speech there is a fronting and deferring, and the estimate is: He sent down upon His servant the Book, upright, and did not make for Him crookedness. Then He, glory be to Him, wished to explain what He had summarised in His saying ﴿qayyiman﴾, so He said: ﴿to warn of severe punishment﴾. The one warned is omitted for knowledge of him together with the intention of generality; the meaning is: to warn the disbelievers.

The ﴿ba's (بَأْسًا)﴾ means punishment, and the meaning of ﴿min ladunhu﴾ is: proceeding from Him, descending from His presence.

Abu Bakr narrated from 'Asim that he recited ﴿min ladunihi﴾ (مِن لَدُنِهِ) with a hint of the dammah on the dal, and with a kasra on the nun and the ha'. This is the dialect of the Kilab.

Abu Zayd narrated from all the readers the fatha on the lam, the damma on the dal, and sukun on the nun (مِن لَدُنْهُ). ﴿And gives good news to the believers who do righteous deeds﴾: it has been read ﴿yubashshiru﴾ with tashdid and with takhfif, and the relative clause was given the same relative clause mentioned earlier, because the basis of the acceptance of deeds is faith. ﴿That they will have a good reward﴾, which is Paradise, while they are ﴿remaining therein﴾, meaning: in that reward, ﴿forever﴾, meaning: a lasting stay with no cessation. The placing of the warning before the good news is to show complete concern for restraining the disbelievers.

Then He repeated the warning and mentioned the one warned specifically, and omitted what is warned of, which is the severe punishment, since it had already been mentioned. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿All praise belongs to Allah, who sent down the Book to His servant and did not make in it any crookedness﴾ ﴿a upright (qayyim) [book], to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good news to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward﴾ ﴿remaining therein forever﴾ ﴿and to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."﴾ ﴿They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they say nothing but a lie.﴾ ﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief over their footsteps if they do not believe in this message.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed.﴾ ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it into barren dust.﴾

He taught His servants how to praise Him for the bounties He pours upon them. The description with the relative pronoun indicates that what is in the relative clause is the cause of what precedes it. The reason that the sending down of the Book, which is the Qur'an, is a blessing upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is that through it he came to know the secrets of monotheism (tawhid), the conditions of the angels and the prophets, and the manner of the legal rulings (ahkam shar'iyyah) by which Allah worshipped him and worshipped his community. Likewise, for the servants, the sending down of the Book upon their prophet was a blessing for them, for the same reason we have mentioned concerning the Prophet.

﴿And did not make in it any crookedness (iwaj)﴾, meaning: no crookedness of any kind of defect in wording or meaning. The word ﴿iwaj﴾ with a kasra (ʿiwaj) is used for meanings, and with a fatha (ʿawaj) for physical things. So it has been said, and it is objected to by His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿You will not see in it any crookedness or unevenness﴾ [Ta-Ha: 107], meaning the mountains, which are physical things.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning in the verse is: He did not place in it any contradiction, as He said: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction﴾ [al-Nisa': 82].

And qayyim means: the straight one that has no deviation; or the one that manages the religious and worldly welfare of the servants; or the one that is a guardian over the heavenly books before it, dominating them. According to the first meaning, it is an emphasis of what the negation of crookedness indicates, for something that appears straight may not be free of the slightest crookedness in reality. The accusative of ﴿qayyiman﴾ is by a hidden verb, meaning: He made it qayyim. The author of al-Kashshaf (Zamakhshari's commentary) prevented it from being a circumstantial state (hal) of "the Book," because His saying ﴿and did not make﴾ is conjoined to ﴿sent down﴾, so it falls within the scope of the relative clause; thus making it a state of "the Book" would separate the state from its owner by part of the relative clause.

Al-Isfahani said: They are two successive states, except that the first is a clause and the second is a single word. This is correct, because His saying ﴿and did not make﴾ was not conjoined to what precedes it; rather the waw is for the state, so there is no separation between the state and its owner by part of the relative clause.

It has also been said that ﴿qayyiman﴾ is a state of the pronoun in ﴿did not make for Him﴾. And it has been said: in the speech there is a fronting and deferring, and the estimate is: He sent down upon His servant the Book, upright, and did not make for Him crookedness. Then He, glory be to Him, wished to explain what He had summarised in His saying ﴿qayyiman﴾, so He said: ﴿to warn of severe punishment﴾. The one warned is omitted for knowledge of him together with the intention of generality; the meaning is: to warn the disbelievers.

The ﴿ba's (بَأْسًا)﴾ means punishment, and the meaning of ﴿min ladunhu﴾ is: proceeding from Him, descending from His presence.

Abu Bakr narrated from 'Asim that he recited ﴿min ladunihi﴾ (مِن لَدُنِهِ) with a hint of the dammah on the dal, and with a kasra on the nun and the ha'. This is the dialect of the Kilab.

Abu Zayd narrated from all the readers the fatha on the lam, the damma on the dal, and sukun on the nun (مِن لَدُنْهُ). ﴿And gives good news to the believers who do righteous deeds﴾: it has been read ﴿yubashshiru﴾ with tashdid and with takhfif, and the relative clause was given the same relative clause mentioned earlier, because the basis of the acceptance of deeds is faith. ﴿That they will have a good reward﴾, which is Paradise, while they are ﴿remaining therein﴾, meaning: in that reward, ﴿forever﴾, meaning: a lasting stay with no cessation. The placing of the warning before the good news is to show complete concern for restraining the disbelievers.

Then He repeated the warning and mentioned the one warned specifically, and omitted what is warned of, which is the severe punishment, since it had already been mentioned. He said: ﴿and to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."﴾ They are the Jews, the Christians, and some of the disbelievers of Quraysh, who say that the angels are the daughters of Allah. So He, glory be to Him, first mentioned a universal proposition, which is the warning of disbelievers in general, then He followed it with a specific proposition which is a part of the particulars of that universal, to draw attention to it being the greatest of the particulars of that universal. This indicates that attributing a son to Allah, glory be to Him, is the most hideous kind of disbelief.

﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾, meaning: of the son, or of Allah taking him. The ﴿min (مِن)﴾ is extra for emphasis of the negation, and the clause is in a place of accusative as a state, or it is a new sentence; the meaning is: they have no knowledge of that at all. ﴿Nor did their fathers﴾ have knowledge; rather, in this claim of theirs they were in error, and their children imitated them, so they all went astray. ﴿Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾: the accusative of ﴿kalimatan (كَلِمَةً)﴾ is as a specification (tamyiz), and it has been read in the nominative as the subject.

Al-Farra' said: That word was great as a word.

Al-Zajjaj said: Their statement was great as a word, and what is meant by this word is their saying: "Allah has taken a son."

Then He described the word with His saying ﴿that comes out of their mouths﴾, and the benefit of this description is to magnify their audacity in uttering it. What comes out of the mouth is only mere breath, but since letters and sounds are qualities subsisting in the breath, He attributed to the state what belongs to the place. Then He increased in disparaging what had occurred from them and said: ﴿they say nothing but a lie﴾, meaning: they say nothing but a lie with no room for truth in it in any way.

Then He consoled His Messenger (ﷺ) with His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief over their footsteps.﴾ Al-Akhfash and al-Farra' said: al-bakhʿ (البَخْعُ) is exertion.

Al-Kisa'i said: I exhausted the land by farming when you make it weak through continuous ploughing, and the man exhausted himself when he wore it out.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: its meaning is: destroying yourself, and from it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: "O you, the one whom grief has destroyed (al-bakhi' al-wajd) himself." So the meaning according to these statements is: perhaps you would exhaust yourself, or weaken it, or destroy it, over their footsteps, meaning after their departure and after their turning away and aversion, ﴿if they do not believe in this message﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. The answer of the condition is omitted, and what precedes it indicates it.

It has been read with fatha on the ﴿an (أنْ)﴾, meaning: because they did not believe, ﴿out of grief (asafan)﴾, meaning: anger and sorrow. It is either an object of purpose or a verbal noun in the place of a state. So said al-Zajjaj.

﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it﴾: this sentence is a new beginning.

The meaning is: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth, of what is fit to be an adornment for it, of animals, plants, and inanimate things, as in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿He it is who created for you all that is on the earth﴾. The accusative of ﴿zinatan (زِينَةً)﴾ is that it is the second object of ﴿ja'ala (جَعَلَ)﴾. The lam in ﴿that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed﴾ is connected to ﴿ja'alna (جَعَلْنا)﴾, and it is either for purpose or for consequence. What is meant by the trial is that He, glory be to Him, treats them with a treatment which, if it came from other than Him, would be of the kind of trial and examination.

Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿Ayyuhum (أيُّهم)﴾ is raised as the subject, except that its form is the form of a question, and the meaning is: that We may examine: is this one better in deed, or that one? Al-Hasan said: ﴿ayyuhum (أيُّهم)﴾ means: which of them is more ascetic. Muqatil said: which of them is most righteous in what he has been given of knowledge.

Then He, glory be to Him, informed that He will annihilate and destroy all of that, so He said: ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it into barren dust (sa'idan juruzan)﴾, meaning: indeed, We will make what is upon it of this adornment, at the end of the life of this world, into dust.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-sa'id (الصَّعِيدُ) is the level of the earth.

Al-Zajjaj said: It is the road which has no vegetation in it.

Al-Farra' said: al-juruz (الجُرُزُ) is the land in which there is no vegetation. From their saying: a woman who is jurraz (جُرازٌ) when she is a great eater; a sword which is jurraz when it is cutting off completely; and the locust, the sheep and the camels "jarazat" the land when they have eaten what is on it.

Dhu al-Rummah said: "The pressing and the grazing (al-ijraz) have emptied what is in their bellies."

The meaning of the structure is: Do not grieve, O Muhammad, over what has happened from these people of denial. Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for the testing of their deeds, and indeed, We will remove that at the completion of the life of this world, and We will recompense them: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.

Al-Shawkani, Fath al-Qadir, on Surah 18, verses 1–8 (part 2 of 2):

It has been related by Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh, through the chain of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who sent down to His servant the Book﴾ (the verse), that he said: He sent down the Book as "upright" (ʿadlan qayyiman), ﴿and has not made in it any deviance﴾ meaning, ambiguity (multabisan).

Ibn al-Mundhir related from al-Dahhak regarding (qayyiman) that he said: "Straight" (mustaqiman).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah regarding (min ladunhu) that it means: from Him (min ʿindihi).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi regarding (hasanan), meaning Paradise, ﴿and to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son"﴾. He said: They are the Jews and the Christians.

Ibn Mardawayh also related, "from Ibn Abbas, who said: ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabiʿah, Abu Jahl, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib and Abu al-Bukhturi gathered with a group of the Quraysh, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been deeply grieved by what he saw of his people's opposition to him and their rejection of the counsel he brought, which saddened him greatly. Thereupon Allah, glorified is He, sent down: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them﴾."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding (bakhiʿun nafsaka) that it means: "Killing yourself" (qatilun nafsaka).

ʿAbd ibn Humayd related from Mujahid the like of this, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi the like of this.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid regarding (asafan) that he said: "Distress" (jazʿan).

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah regarding (asafan) that he said: "Sorrow" (huznan).

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh related, through the chain of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is upon the earth an adornment for it﴾, that he said: "The men."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from his own statement, the like of this.

Abu Nasr al-Sijzi in al-Ibanah related, through the chain of Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "The scholars are the adornment of the earth."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan who said: They are the men who worship and labor for Allah through obedience.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim in al-Tarikh and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Umar who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿That He may test you [as to] which of you is best in deed﴾. I said: 'What is the meaning of that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'That He may test you as to which of you is best in intellect, most scrupulous regarding the prohibitions of Allah, and quickest in obedience to Allah.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah who said: "to test them" (liyakhtabirahum), ﴿which of them is best in deed﴾: "which of them is most complete in intellect."

He related from al-Hasan, ﴿which of them is best in deed﴾, who said: "The one most abstaining from this world," and he also related from al-Thawri who said: "The most ascetic of them in this world."

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it a barren wasteland (saʿidan juruzan)﴾, that he said: "He destroys everything and annihilates it."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah who said: "The saʿid is the dust, and the mountains in which there is no crop."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan who said: "By juruz he means the ruined."

Abu Zayd narrated from all the readers the fatha on the lam, the damma on the dal, and sukun on the nun (مِن لَدُنْهُ). ﴿And gives good news to the believers who do righteous deeds﴾: it has been read ﴿yubashshiru﴾ with tashdid and with takhfif, and the relative clause was given the same relative clause mentioned earlier, because the basis of the acceptance of deeds is faith. ﴿That they will have a good reward﴾, which is Paradise, while they are ﴿remaining therein﴾, meaning: in that reward, ﴿forever﴾, meaning: a lasting stay with no cessation. The placing of the warning before the good news is to show complete concern for restraining the disbelievers.

Then He repeated the warning and mentioned the one warned specifically, and omitted what is warned of, which is the severe punishment, since it had already been mentioned. He said: ﴿and to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."﴾ They are the Jews, the Christians, and some of the disbelievers of Quraysh, who say that the angels are the daughters of Allah. So He, glory be to Him, first mentioned a universal proposition, which is the warning of disbelievers in general, then He followed it with a specific proposition which is a part of the particulars of that universal, to draw attention to it being the greatest of the particulars of that universal. This indicates that attributing a son to Allah, glory be to Him, is the most hideous kind of disbelief.

﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾, meaning: of the son, or of Allah taking him. The ﴿min (مِن)﴾ is extra for emphasis of the negation, and the clause is in a place of accusative as a state, or it is a new sentence; the meaning is: they have no knowledge of that at all. ﴿Nor did their fathers﴾ have knowledge; rather, in this claim of theirs they were in error, and their children imitated them, so they all went astray. ﴿Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾: the accusative of ﴿kalimatan (كَلِمَةً)﴾ is as a specification (tamyiz), and it has been read in the nominative as the subject.

Al-Farra' said: That word was great as a word.

Al-Zajjaj said: Their statement was great as a word, and what is meant by this word is their saying: "Allah has taken a son."

Then He described the word with His saying ﴿that comes out of their mouths﴾, and the benefit of this description is to magnify their audacity in uttering it. What comes out of the mouth is only mere breath, but since letters and sounds are qualities subsisting in the breath, He attributed to the state what belongs to the place. Then He increased in disparaging what had occurred from them and said: ﴿they say nothing but a lie﴾, meaning: they say nothing but a lie with no room for truth in it in any way.

Then He consoled His Messenger (ﷺ) with His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief over their footsteps.﴾ Al-Akhfash and al-Farra' said: al-bakhʿ (البَخْعُ) is exertion.

Al-Kisa'i said: I exhausted the land by farming when you make it weak through continuous ploughing, and the man exhausted himself when he wore it out.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: its meaning is: destroying yourself, and from it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: "O you, the one whom grief has destroyed (al-bakhi' al-wajd) himself." So the meaning according to these statements is: perhaps you would exhaust yourself, or weaken it, or destroy it, over their footsteps, meaning after their departure and after their turning away and aversion, ﴿if they do not believe in this message﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. The answer of the condition is omitted, and what precedes it indicates it.

It has been read with fatha on the ﴿an (أنْ)﴾, meaning: because they did not believe, ﴿out of grief (asafan)﴾, meaning: anger and sorrow. It is either an object of purpose or a verbal noun in the place of a state. So said al-Zajjaj.

﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it﴾: this sentence is a new beginning.

The meaning is: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth, of what is fit to be an adornment for it, of animals, plants, and inanimate things, as in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿He it is who created for you all that is on the earth﴾. The accusative of ﴿zinatan (زِينَةً)﴾ is that it is the second object of ﴿ja'ala (جَعَلَ)﴾. The lam in ﴿that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed﴾ is connected to ﴿ja'alna (جَعَلْنا)﴾, and it is either for purpose or for consequence. What is meant by the trial is that He, glory be to Him, treats them with a treatment which, if it came from other than Him, would be of the kind of trial and examination.

Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿Ayyuhum (أيُّهم)﴾ is raised as the subject, except that its form is the form of a question, and the meaning is: that We may examine: is this one better in deed, or that one? Al-Zajjaj said: It is the road which has no vegetation in it.

Al-Shawkani, Fath al-Qadir, on Surah 18, verses 1–8 (part 2 of 2):

It has been related by Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh, through the chain of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who sent down to His servant the Book﴾ (the verse), that he said: He sent down the Book as "upright" (ʿadlan qayyiman), ﴿and has not made in it any deviance﴾ meaning, ambiguity (multabisan).

Ibn al-Mundhir related from al-Dahhak regarding (qayyiman) that he said: "Straight" (mustaqiman).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah regarding (min ladunhu) that it means: from Him (min ʿindihi).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi regarding (hasanan), meaning Paradise, ﴿and to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son"﴾. He said: They are the Jews and the Christians.

Ibn Mardawayh also related, "from Ibn Abbas, who said: ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabiʿah, Abu Jahl, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib and Abu al-Bukhturi gathered with a group of the Quraysh, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been deeply grieved by what he saw of his people's opposition to him and their rejection of the counsel he brought, which saddened him greatly. Thereupon Allah, glorified is He, sent down: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them﴾."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding (bakhiʿun nafsaka) that it means: "Killing yourself" (qatilun nafsaka).

ʿAbd ibn Humayd related from Mujahid the like of this, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi the like of this.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid regarding (asafan) that he said: "Distress" (jazʿan).

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah regarding (asafan) that he said: "Sorrow" (huznan).

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh related, through the chain of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is upon the earth an adornment for it﴾, that he said: "The men."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from his own statement, the like of this.

Abu Nasr al-Sijzi in al-Ibanah related, through the chain of Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "The scholars are the adornment of the earth."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan who said: They are the men who worship and labor for Allah through obedience.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim in al-Tarikh and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Umar who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿That He may test you [as to] which of you is best in deed﴾. I said: 'What is the meaning of that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'That He may test you as to which of you is best in intellect, most scrupulous regarding the prohibitions of Allah, and quickest in obedience to Allah.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah who said: "to test them" (liyakhtabirahum), ﴿which of them is best in deed﴾: "which of them is most complete in intellect."

He related from al-Hasan, ﴿which of them is best in deed﴾, who said: "The one most abstaining from this world," and he also related from al-Thawri who said: "The most ascetic of them in this world."

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it a barren wasteland (saʿidan juruzan)﴾, that he said: "He destroys everything and annihilates it."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah who said: "The saʿid is the dust, and the mountains in which there is no crop."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan who said: "By juruz he means the ruined."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 18, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

Al-Qurtubi said: It is Meccan according to the agreement of all the exegetes (mufassirun).

It is narrated from a group that the beginning of the surah was revealed in Medina, up to His saying ﴿jurzan﴾ (barren). But the first view is more sound. End of quotation.

Among those who said that the whole surah is Meccan is Ibn 'Abbas, which al-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him. Among them also is Ibn al-Zubayr, which Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him.

Hadiths have come concerning its virtue, among them what Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and others transmitted from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever memorises ten verses from the beginning of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal (the Antichrist)."

Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Hibban transmitted, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the last ten verses of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal."

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others transmitted, from al-Bara', who said: "A man recited Surat al-Kahf while there was an animal in the house, and it began to shy. He looked and saw a mist or a cloud that had covered him. He mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'Recite, so-and-so, for tranquillity (sakinah) descended for the Qur'an.'" This man who was reciting was Usayd ibn Hudayr, as al-Tabarani made clear.

al-Tirmidhi transmitted and graded it sound, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites three verses from the beginning of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal." Regarding the recitation of ten verses from its beginning or from its end, there are hadiths.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah transmitted, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites al-Kahf on Friday, he is protected until eight days from every trial that occurs. If the Dajjal emerges, he will be protected from him."

al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Hakim (who graded it sound), Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi and al-Diya' transmitted, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf, it will be a light for him from his station to Makkah. Whoever recites ten verses from its end, then the Dajjal emerges, he will not harm him."

al-Hakim transmitted and graded it sound, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf on the day of Friday, there will be light shining for him between the two Fridays."

al-Bayhaqi also transmitted it in al-Sunan from this route and from another route.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf on the day of Friday, a light will shine for him from beneath his foot up to the clouds of the sky, illuminating for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be forgiven what is between the two Fridays."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I inform you of a surah whose greatness fills what is between the heaven and the earth, and for its writer is a reward like that? Whoever recites it on Friday, he will be forgiven what is between him and the next Friday, with an addition of three days. And whoever recites its last five verses when he sleeps, Allah will raise him at whatever hour of the night he wishes." They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "The surah of the People of the Cave."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The house in which Surat al-Kahf is recited, a devil will not enter it that night." There are other hadiths and reports on this subject, and what we have cited is sufficient.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Likewise, for the servants, the sending down of the Book upon their prophet was a blessing for them, for the same reason we have mentioned concerning the Prophet.

According to the first meaning, it is an emphasis of what the negation of crookedness indicates, for something that appears straight may not be free of the slightest crookedness in reality. The accusative of ﴿qayyiman﴾ is by a hidden verb, meaning: He made it qayyim. Abu Nasr al-Sijzi in al-Ibanah related, through the chain of Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "The scholars are the adornment of the earth."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan who said: They are the men who worship and labor for Allah through obedience.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim in al-Tarikh and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Umar who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿That He may test you [as to] which of you is best in deed﴾. I said: 'What is the meaning of that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'That He may test you as to which of you is best in intellect, most scrupulous regarding the prohibitions of Allah, and quickest in obedience to Allah.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah who said: "to test them" (liyakhtabirahum), ﴿which of them is best in deed﴾: "which of them is most complete in intellect."

He related from al-Hasan, ﴿which of them is best in deed﴾, who said: "The one most abstaining from this world," and he also related from al-Thawri who said: "The most ascetic of them in this world."

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it a barren wasteland (saʿidan juruzan)﴾, that he said: "He destroys everything and annihilates it."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah who said: "The saʿid is the dust, and the mountains in which there is no crop."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan who said: "By juruz he means the ruined."

Al-Qurtubi said: It is Meccan according to the agreement of all the exegetes (mufassirun).

It is narrated from a group that the beginning of the surah was revealed in Medina, up to His saying ﴿jurzan﴾ (barren). But the first view is more sound. End of quotation.

Among those who said that the whole surah is Meccan is Ibn 'Abbas, which al-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him. Among them also is Ibn al-Zubayr, which Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him.

Hadiths have come concerning its virtue, among them what Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and others transmitted from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever memorises ten verses from the beginning of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal (the Antichrist)."

Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Hibban transmitted, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the last ten verses of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal."

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others transmitted, from al-Bara', who said: "A man recited Surat al-Kahf while there was an animal in the house, and it began to shy. He looked and saw a mist or a cloud that had covered him. He mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'Recite, so-and-so, for tranquillity (sakinah) descended for the Qur'an.'" This man who was reciting was Usayd ibn Hudayr, as al-Tabarani made clear.

al-Tirmidhi transmitted and graded it sound, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites three verses from the beginning of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal." Regarding the recitation of ten verses from its beginning or from its end, there are hadiths.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah transmitted, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites al-Kahf on Friday, he is protected until eight days from every trial that occurs. If the Dajjal emerges, he will be protected from him."

al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Hakim (who graded it sound), Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi and al-Diya' transmitted, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf, it will be a light for him from his station to Makkah. Whoever recites ten verses from its end, then the Dajjal emerges, he will not harm him."

al-Hakim transmitted and graded it sound, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf on the day of Friday, there will be light shining for him between the two Fridays."

al-Bayhaqi also transmitted it in al-Sunan from this route and from another route.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf on the day of Friday, a light will shine for him from beneath his foot up to the clouds of the sky, illuminating for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be forgiven what is between the two Fridays."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I inform you of a surah whose greatness fills what is between the heaven and the earth, and for its writer is a reward like that? Whoever recites it on Friday, he will be forgiven what is between him and the next Friday, with an addition of three days. And whoever recites its last five verses when he sleeps, Allah will raise him at whatever hour of the night he wishes." They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "The surah of the People of the Cave."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿All praise belongs to Allah, who sent down the Book to His servant and did not make in it any crookedness﴾ ﴿a upright (qayyim) [book], to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good news to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward﴾ ﴿remaining therein forever﴾ ﴿and to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."﴾ ﴿They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they say nothing but a lie.﴾ ﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief over their footsteps if they do not believe in this message.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed.﴾ ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it into barren dust.﴾

He taught His servants how to praise Him for the bounties He pours upon them. The description with the relative pronoun indicates that what is in the relative clause is the cause of what precedes it. The reason that the sending down of the Book, which is the Qur'an, is a blessing upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is that through it he came to know the secrets of monotheism (tawhid), the conditions of the angels and the prophets, and the manner of the legal rulings (ahkam shar'iyyah) by which Allah worshipped him and worshipped his community. Likewise, for the servants, the sending down of the Book upon their prophet was a blessing for them, for the same reason we have mentioned concerning the Prophet.

﴿And did not make in it any crookedness (iwaj)﴾, meaning: no crookedness of any kind of defect in wording or meaning. The word ﴿iwaj﴾ with a kasra (ʿiwaj) is used for meanings, and with a fatha (ʿawaj) for physical things. So it has been said, and it is objected to by His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿You will not see in it any crookedness or unevenness﴾ [Ta-Ha: 107], meaning the mountains, which are physical things.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning in the verse is: He did not place in it any contradiction, as He said: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction﴾ [al-Nisa': 82].

And qayyim means: the straight one that has no deviation; or the one that manages the religious and worldly welfare of the servants; or the one that is a guardian over the heavenly books before it, dominating them. According to the first meaning, it is an emphasis of what the negation of crookedness indicates, for something that appears straight may not be free of the slightest crookedness in reality. The accusative of ﴿qayyiman﴾ is by a hidden verb, meaning: He made it qayyim. The author of al-Kashshaf (Zamakhshari's commentary) prevented it from being a circumstantial state (hal) of "the Book," because His saying ﴿and did not make﴾ is conjoined to ﴿sent down﴾, so it falls within the scope of the relative clause; thus making it a state of "the Book" would separate the state from its owner by part of the relative clause.

Al-Isfahani said: They are two successive states, except that the first is a clause and the second is a single word. This is correct, because His saying ﴿and did not make﴾ was not conjoined to what precedes it; rather the waw is for the state, so there is no separation between the state and its owner by part of the relative clause.

It has also been said that ﴿qayyiman﴾ is a state of the pronoun in ﴿did not make for Him﴾. And it has been said: in the speech there is a fronting and deferring, and the estimate is: He sent down upon His servant the Book, upright, and did not make for Him crookedness. Then He, glory be to Him, wished to explain what He had summarised in His saying ﴿qayyiman﴾, so He said: ﴿to warn of severe punishment﴾. The one warned is omitted for knowledge of him together with the intention of generality; the meaning is: to warn the disbelievers.

The ﴿ba's (بَأْسًا)﴾ means punishment, and the meaning of ﴿min ladunhu﴾ is: proceeding from Him, descending from His presence.

Abu Bakr narrated from 'Asim that he recited ﴿min ladunihi﴾ (مِن لَدُنِهِ) with a hint of the dammah on the dal, and with a kasra on the nun and the ha'. This is the dialect of the Kilab.

Abu Zayd narrated from all the readers the fatha on the lam, the damma on the dal, and sukun on the nun (مِن لَدُنْهُ). ﴿And gives good news to the believers who do righteous deeds﴾: it has been read ﴿yubashshiru﴾ with tashdid and with takhfif, and the relative clause was given the same relative clause mentioned earlier, because the basis of the acceptance of deeds is faith. ﴿That they will have a good reward﴾, which is Paradise, while they are ﴿remaining therein﴾, meaning: in that reward, ﴿forever﴾, meaning: a lasting stay with no cessation. The placing of the warning before the good news is to show complete concern for restraining the disbelievers.

Then He repeated the warning and mentioned the one warned specifically, and omitted what is warned of, which is the severe punishment, since it had already been mentioned. He said: ﴿and to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."﴾ They are the Jews, the Christians, and some of the disbelievers of Quraysh, who say that the angels are the daughters of Allah. So He, glory be to Him, first mentioned a universal proposition, which is the warning of disbelievers in general, then He followed it with a specific proposition which is a part of the particulars of that universal, to draw attention to it being the greatest of the particulars of that universal. This indicates that attributing a son to Allah, glory be to Him, is the most hideous kind of disbelief.

﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾, meaning: of the son, or of Allah taking him. The ﴿min (مِن)﴾ is extra for emphasis of the negation, and the clause is in a place of accusative as a state, or it is a new sentence; the meaning is: they have no knowledge of that at all. ﴿Nor did their fathers﴾ have knowledge; rather, in this claim of theirs they were in error, and their children imitated them, so they all went astray. ﴿Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾: the accusative of ﴿kalimatan (كَلِمَةً)﴾ is as a specification (tamyiz), and it has been read in the nominative as the subject.

Al-Farra' said: That word was great as a word.

Al-Zajjaj said: Their statement was great as a word, and what is meant by this word is their saying: "Allah has taken a son."

Then He described the word with His saying ﴿that comes out of their mouths﴾, and the benefit of this description is to magnify their audacity in uttering it. What comes out of the mouth is only mere breath, but since letters and sounds are qualities subsisting in the breath, He attributed to the state what belongs to the place. Then He increased in disparaging what had occurred from them and said: ﴿they say nothing but a lie﴾, meaning: they say nothing but a lie with no room for truth in it in any way.

Then He consoled His Messenger (ﷺ) with His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief over their footsteps.﴾ Al-Akhfash and al-Farra' said: al-bakhʿ (البَخْعُ) is exertion.

Al-Kisa'i said: I exhausted the land by farming when you make it weak through continuous ploughing, and the man exhausted himself when he wore it out.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: its meaning is: destroying yourself, and from it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: "O you, the one whom grief has destroyed (al-bakhi' al-wajd) himself." So the meaning according to these statements is: perhaps you would exhaust yourself, or weaken it, or destroy it, over their footsteps, meaning after their departure and after their turning away and aversion, ﴿if they do not believe in this message﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. The answer of the condition is omitted, and what precedes it indicates it.

It has been read with fatha on the ﴿an (أنْ)﴾, meaning: because they did not believe, ﴿out of grief (asafan)﴾, meaning: anger and sorrow. It is either an object of purpose or a verbal noun in the place of a state. So said al-Zajjaj.

﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it﴾: this sentence is a new beginning.

The meaning is: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth, of what is fit to be an adornment for it, of animals, plants, and inanimate things, as in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿He it is who created for you all that is on the earth﴾. The accusative of ﴿zinatan (زِينَةً)﴾ is that it is the second object of ﴿ja'ala (جَعَلَ)﴾. The lam in ﴿that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed﴾ is connected to ﴿ja'alna (جَعَلْنا)﴾, and it is either for purpose or for consequence. What is meant by the trial is that He, glory be to Him, treats them with a treatment which, if it came from other than Him, would be of the kind of trial and examination.

Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿Ayyuhum (أيُّهم)﴾ is raised as the subject, except that its form is the form of a question, and the meaning is: that We may examine: is this one better in deed, or that one? Al-Hasan said: ﴿ayyuhum (أيُّهم)﴾ means: which of them is more ascetic. Muqatil said: which of them is most righteous in what he has been given of knowledge.

Then He, glory be to Him, informed that He will annihilate and destroy all of that, so He said: ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it into barren dust (sa'idan juruzan)﴾, meaning: indeed, We will make what is upon it of this adornment, at the end of the life of this world, into dust.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-sa'id (الصَّعِيدُ) is the level of the earth.

Al-Zajjaj said: It is the road which has no vegetation in it.

Al-Farra' said: al-juruz (الجُرُزُ) is the land in which there is no vegetation. From their saying: a woman who is jurraz (جُرازٌ) when she is a great eater; a sword which is jurraz when it is cutting off completely; and the locust, the sheep and the camels "jarazat" the land when they have eaten what is on it.

Dhu al-Rummah said: "The pressing and the grazing (al-ijraz) have emptied what is in their bellies."

The meaning of the structure is: Do not grieve, O Muhammad, over what has happened from these people of denial. Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for the testing of their deeds, and indeed, We will remove that at the completion of the life of this world, and We will recompense them: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd related from Mujahid the like of this, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi the like of this.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid regarding (asafan) that he said: "Distress" (jazʿan).

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah regarding (asafan) that he said: "Sorrow" (huznan).

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh related, through the chain of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is upon the earth an adornment for it﴾, that he said: "The men."

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it a barren wasteland (saʿidan juruzan)﴾, that he said: "He destroys everything and annihilates it."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah who said: "The saʿid is the dust, and the mountains in which there is no crop."
